source.title: An Open Problem on Sparse Representations in Unions of Bases

accepted.question_text: Let D be a dictionary formed as a union of q + 1 orthonormal bases, with q at least 2. Let the spark eta(D) be the smallest number of columns of D that are linearly dependent, and let the mutual coherence mu(D) be the largest absolute normalized inner product between distinct columns of D. Two known lower bounds relate spark to mutual coherence: for an arbitrary dictionary, eta(D) >= 1 + 1/mu(D), and for a union of q + 1 orthonormal bases, eta(D) >= (1 + 1/q) / mu(D). Are these lower bounds tight for dictionaries that are unions of several orthonormal bases, in the sense that one can construct such dictionaries where the corresponding lower-bound value is actually achieved?

evidence.quote: Motivated by these open questions, we study the tightness of the estimate (I.1) and the estimate (I.3).
Our results imply that two well-known estimates for the spark are indeed tight.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Further generalization of Theorem I.2 could be considered. For example, the mutual coherence is 1/2 q1 and the number of orthonormal bases is 2 q2 + 1, where q2 is a factor of q1.

evidence.quote: Further generalization of Theorem I.2 could be considered.

trace.notes: Original input was a zbMATH resolver URL. Direct fetch of https://zbmath.org/7555928 returned a Cloudflare challenge. The official zbMATH REST API resolved document 7555928 to the title, DOI 10.1109/TIT.2022.3159100, and arXiv identifier 2109.07782. The arXiv PDF was downloaded and used as the readable primary artifact.

Mapped the PDF structure: abstract and introduction; Background, Motivations, Observations, Contributions, Flowchart, and Outline; matrix and Galois-field constructions; Hadamard matrices; mutually unbiased bases; proofs of main theorems; examples; conclusion. Likely open-question regions were the Motivations and Contributions subsections on page 2 and the conclusion on page 16.
Extracted the open questions about tightness of estimates (I.1) and (I.3). The surrounding source text defines spark eta(D), mutual coherence mu(D), and the two lower bounds.
Extracted the future-direction candidate about generalizing Theorem I.2, but the PDF text extraction renders the formula ambiguously.

Merged the two closely related tightness questions into one self-contained question and expanded eta(D), mu(D), and the two lower-bound statements using definitions and formulas from pages 1-2. Marked solved because the conclusion explicitly says the estimates are tight.
Kept the future-direction candidate in needs_review because the extracted formula '1/2 q1' is ambiguous and cannot be safely rewritten as a self-contained mathematical question without guessing.
The I.1 and I.3 tightness candidates were merged because the source groups them as the motivating open questions and resolves both with the same construction program.
Accepted: the question is self-contained, includes source-defined notation and assumptions, has page-located evidence, and does not rely on source-pointing language.
